transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, the main thing is work. I mean, I’ve been in computer support a long time, so I know what normal policy changes look like, and this isn’t just that. For over a year now, the new ticket rotation and these security audits have been… I don’t know, used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying, “See, it’s just policy,” but logs can be made to tell whatever story they want.

And it’s not like I’m some new guy who doesn’t understand systems—I’ve got a degree, I’ve been doing this for years. Sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked, but that’s why I’m here. I need someone to actually take this seriously.
Have you ever heard, seen, or sensed things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or couldn't confirm—like voices or other unusual perceptions?

No, not voices or seeing things, if that’s what you mean. I mean, I notice things other people don’t pay attention to—like timing, patterns in tickets, who gets copied on emails—but that’s not the same as hearing something that isn’t there. I’ve worked with systems long enough to know when something is off. But, no, I’m not sitting around hearing voices or seeing people who aren’t there.
Outside of work, do you find yourself suspicious of the motives of people close to you—like family or friends—or is this feeling really centered on what's happening at your job?

It’s mostly work. I mean, I don’t sit around thinking my family is plotting against me or anything like that. This is specific—at my job, with the ticket rotation and these so-called security audits.

And I know how that sounds, but I’ve been doing computer support for years, and when a system changes in a certain way and then suddenly the records start making one person look bad, you notice. Management keeps saying it’s just policy and showing logs, but logs aren’t neutral if the process behind them is being used to build a paper trail. That’s really why I’m here—I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to take that seriously.

Before this situation at your current job started about a year ago, would you say you generally had this same level of suspicion or distrust toward coworkers, bosses, or others in your life, even going back to your 20s?

No, I wouldn’t say it goes back that far. I mean, I’ve had bosses I didn’t like—who hasn’t?—and there were coworkers over the years who played office politics, but this level of… watching the patterns and feeling like something was being set up, that really started with the hybrid schedule and the after-hours ticket changes.

That was about a year and two months ago now. And it’s funny, because at first I thought, okay, everyone’s adjusting after the schedule change, maybe the workload’s just uneven. But then the tickets, the audits, the timing of it all—sorry, I’m getting into the weeds again. But no, before that, I wouldn’t say I was suspicious like this.

Aside from the stress this situation at work is causing, has your day-to-day functioning changed—like your ability to concentrate, keep up with personal responsibilities, or engage socially with friends and family?

I mean, it’s stressful, yes, but I’m not falling apart in the rest of my life. I still keep the house in order, pay the bills, help my wife with things. I’m not sitting there with unpaid envelopes piling up on the counter or anything like that.

And at work, the technical part—I still do that. I can troubleshoot, document, fix what needs fixing. Nobody’s saying my actual work is sloppy or that I’m disorganized. The problem is more that the way the tickets and audits are being handled makes it look a certain way, and then you spend half your mental energy trying to figure out why that pattern keeps happening. But day to day, outside of that issue, I’m functioning.
